thread:
Anna (Docs): Heads-up: we need a short pattern for canonical glossary IDs + snippet placeholders before the migration sweep. Current variance is causing broken links and confusing examples.

Sam (Tech Writer): Agreed. Propose: canonical-id (kebab) for links, display_name for UI, example_param (snake) in python snippets, and a language mapping note.

Diego (SDK): For snippet automation I prefer token form [[GLOSS:canonical-id]] so replace is deterministic. I can add a CI check to fail if unresolved tokens remain.

Matt R: I'll open a gating PR that adds docs/data/glossary_map.csv. Teams should pause snippet PRs until it's in. I'll also add a small grep to find common variants.

Jules P: Can we include a column for aliases (comma-separated)? That helps search redirects and quick grep-driven mapping.

Anna (Docs): Yes. CSV fields: id, display_name, py_example, js_example, aliases. Keep CSV flat to avoid tooling issues. I'll draft a one-paragraph checklist for writers: reference CSV, use [[GLOSS:...]] tokens, include language mapping note, and run link-check locally.

Diego (SDK): Will implement token-replacer script and snippet compile test. Also add a pre-commit hook to warn about bare variants like paramCase.

ci-bot: gating PR #711 opened by Matt R. link-check queued.

Matt R: Please don't merge other snippet changes until #711 passes. I'll mark it as blocking in the PR description.

Sam (Tech Writer): I'll update the migration guide with an example section showing the token pattern and language mapping examples.

ci-bot: gating PR #711 passed link-check and snippet-compile. All green.

Anna (Docs): Great, thanks everyone. Once CSV lands, Diego and I will run a quick repo-wide replacement plan and post the rollout steps.
